headline: IBM takes most of the industry's profit
text: By one estimate IBM earns 41% of the revenue and 69% of the profit of the hundred largest data-processing companies, with a profit margin of 22%, three times the average of the rest. Its computer revenue is about nine times that of the number two, Digital Equipment. Competitors complain to Congress about its power. John Akers takes over as chief executive this year.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_IBM (read 2026-10-03, citing NYT 1985-01-20 'The Daunting Power of I.B.M.'); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Fellows_Akers (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Model M keyboard, 2024

headline: Gorbachev takes over the Soviet Union
text: Mikhail Gorbachev, 54, was chosen on 11 March as general secretary of the Soviet Communist Party, a day after Konstantin Chernenko died. He follows three old and sick leaders who died within two and a half years: Brezhnev, Andropov and Chernenko. The West is trying to work out what the new man wants.
imageCaption: Mikhail Gorbachev, the Soviet Union's new leader, in 1985

headline: Buffett backs Capital Cities' purchase of ABC
text: On 18 March Berkshire agreed to buy three million new shares of Capital Cities Communications at 172.50 dollars each, about 517 million dollars, to help it buy the ABC television network for 3.5 billion dollars. ABC is about four times the size of Capital Cities.
imageCaption: Thomas Murphy, chairman of Capital Cities Communications, New York, 18 March 1985

headline: McDonald's passes 8,000 restaurants and 10 billion dollars in sales
text: Sales of all McDonald's restaurants together reached about 10 billion dollars in 1984, and the company's net income rose to 389 million. It had about 8,300 restaurants at the end of the year, some 1,700 of them outside the United States, in 36 countries.
source: https://archive.org/download/mcdonaldscorpannualreports/mcdonalds1994_djvu.txt (1994 annual report, 11-year summary, read 2026-10-03); yearly change from data/out/mcd.json
imageCaption: McDonald's headquarters, Oak Brook, Illinois
imageCredit: Rob LaRosa from Las Vegas, NV, USA

headline: Coca-Cola changes its formula: New Coke
text: On 23 April Coca-Cola replaced its 99-year-old formula with a sweeter new one. The company says the sweeter drink beat both the old Coke and Pepsi in blind taste tests. Pepsi now has a slightly bigger share of the US market than Coca-Cola's flagship. The company hotline is getting more than 1,500 calls a day, up from about 400, many of them angry.
imageCaption: Coca-Cola chairman Roberto Goizueta (left) and president Donald Keough toast New Coke after presenting it at Lincoln Center, New York, 23 April 1985

headline: Exxon has quietly bought back a tenth of its own shares
text: Since mid-1983 Exxon has spent more than 3.5 billion dollars buying back about 10 percent of its own stock, at an average of about 41 dollars a share against a recent price of about 50, and it shows no sign of stopping. At the same time it keeps a large exploration programme. Fortune calculates that buying its own shares has been a cheaper way to get oil reserves than drilling for them.
imageCaption: Part of Exxon's oil refinery at Linden, New Jersey
imageCredit: Ike Vern for the US EPA Documerica project (US National Archives)

headline: Industrial Bank of Japan, banker to Japan's big industry, joins the game
text: The Industrial Bank of Japan, founded in 1902 as a state bank to finance industry, is a long-term credit bank: it lends for many years to large companies such as steelmakers, shipbuilders and carmakers and funds itself by issuing debentures. Its ordinary income passed 1 trillion yen in 1982, and it holds shares in many of its clients.
imageCaption: The head office of the Industrial Bank of Japan, Tokyo

headline: Zurich's 'unbraked boom' is led by the banks
text: The Zurich stock exchange kept setting records in the last week of June on unusually heavy trading. Measured by the Kreditanstalt index Swiss shares are up nearly 20% this half-year, about as much as Amsterdam and Paris and well ahead of London and Tokyo. Dealers say the boom will last as long as the leading shares, above all the banks and insurers, keep leading it; Bankverein and Kreditanstalt bearer shares were marked up sharply on big volume, and Bankgesellschaft reached a new high for the year.
source: Neue Zürcher Zeitung, 29 June 1985, p. 23 ('Zürcher Börse vom 24. Juni bis zum 28. Juni: Ungebremste Hausse'), scan data/manual/scans/nzz/NZZ_1985-06-29.pdf (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The Zurich head office of the Schweizerischer Bankverein on Paradeplatz

headline: Daimler takes control of Dornier as foreigners pile into German shares
text: After buying all of the engine maker MTU from MAN in February, Daimler-Benz signed contracts in April and May, with help from the state government of Baden-Württemberg, to buy a majority of the aerospace company Dornier, about 66% for around 500 million marks. Foreign investors are buying German blue chips on the back of a strong economy and rising profits, and Daimler is their favourite; its price rose by about a quarter between the end of April and the end of June.
source: Mercedes-Benz Classic, Illustrated Chronicle 1985 ('MTU becomes subsidiary', 14 February 1985; 'Daimler-Benz acquires Dornier shares', 23 April and 15 May 1985), https://mercedes-benz-publicarchive.com/marsClassic/en/instance/ko.xhtml?oid=4910873&viewType=list (read 2026-10-03); Der Spiegel 31/1995, https://www.spiegel.de/spiegel/print/d-9205712.html (read 2026-10-03); Die Zeit, 'Börsen-Report: Daimler ist Spitze', 30 August 1985, https://www.zeit.de/1985/36/daimler-ist-spitze (read 2026-10-03); data/manual/mercedes.csv header (1985-05 left out) (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: A Dornier Do 228 commuter aircraft, built by Dornier, a company Daimler-Benz took control of in 1985

headline: Old Coke comes back as Coca-Cola Classic
text: On 11 July, 79 days after the change, Coca-Cola announced that the original formula will return under the name Coca-Cola Classic, sold next to the new Coke. The company had received more than 40,000 angry calls and letters. Sales had actually been up 8% on the year before.
imageCaption: Cans of New Coke and Coca-Cola Classic on display at the news conference announcing the return of the old formula, Atlanta, 11 July 1985

headline: Live Aid, and Boris Becker wins Wimbledon at 17
text: On 13 July concerts at Wembley in London and in Philadelphia raised money for famine relief in Ethiopia and were watched by an estimated 1.9 billion people. Earlier in July the unseeded West German Boris Becker beat Kevin Curren in the Wimbledon final. At 17 years and 227 days he is the youngest men's champion ever and the first German to win the title.
imageCaption: The stage at Live Aid, JFK Stadium, Philadelphia, 13 July 1985

headline: Back to the Future opens in cinemas
text: Back to the Future opened in American cinemas on 3 July and took 11.3 million dollars in its first weekend, the most of any film. Michael J. Fox plays a teenager who travels back to 1955 in a time machine built from a DeLorean car.

headline: Foreign buyers send BMW shares soaring
text: Foreign investors have discovered German shares, reacting late to the good economic news and rising profits of big German companies. Daimler reached new record highs this month after three years of rising prices, and BMW and Porsche shares made unusually large gains.
source: Die Zeit, 'Börsen-Report: Daimler ist Spitze', 30 August 1985, https://www.zeit.de/1985/36/daimler-ist-spitze (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The BMW headquarters tower, the Vierzylinder, Munich

headline: Steve Jobs leaves Apple
text: On 17 September Steve Jobs, Apple's co-founder and chairman, resigned. In the spring the board had backed chief executive John Sculley, hired from PepsiCo in 1983, when he took the Macintosh division away from Jobs. Five senior employees are leaving with Jobs to start a new company, and Jobs has sold nearly all of his Apple shares.
imageCaption: Steve Jobs receives the National Technology Medal from President Reagan, White House, February 1985
imageCredit: President (1981-1989 : Reagan). White House Photographic Off

headline: Plaza Accord: the rich countries push the dollar down
text: On 22 September the finance ministers of the US, Japan, West Germany, France and Britain agreed at the Plaza Hotel in New York to push the dollar down, after it had gained about 50% against their currencies since 1980. The dollar bought about 242 yen on 20 September and about 217 yen at the end of the month. Japan's exporters, whose goods get dearer abroad, are the most exposed.
imageCaption: The Plaza Hotel, New York, where the finance ministers met on 22 September 1985

headline: Forbes: Sam Walton is the richest man in America
text: Forbes magazine's new list of the 400 richest Americans puts Wal-Mart founder Sam Walton at the top, with an estimated 2.8 billion dollars, almost all of it in Wal-Mart shares. The Walton family holds 54 million shares. Wal-Mart has about 750 stores in 19 states and expects sales of about 6.2 billion dollars this year.
imageCaption: Sam Walton with one of his bird dogs and his red-and-white 1979 Ford F-150 pickup

headline: Swiss shares rush to new peaks
text: After a dip in September, Swiss share indexes, including the Kreditanstalt's own index, climbed to new records in October on very heavy volume. Domestic and foreign buyers are active, registered shares of the blue chips are in strong demand, and the franc firmed further against the dollar.
source: Neue Zürcher Zeitung, 30 November 1985, p. 23 ('Zürcher Börse vom 25. bis zum 29. November: Im Eiltempo zu neuen Gipfeln'), scan data/manual/scans/nzz/NZZ_1985-11-30.pdf (read 2026-10-03); data/raw/fred/DEXSZUS.csv (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Traders shout their orders at the ring of the Zurich stock exchange

headline: Intel gives up memory chips and launches the 386
text: On 10 October Intel told its staff that it is leaving the market for DRAM memory chips, the product it pioneered in 1970, after falling prices, slumping demand and a glut of supply, much of it from Japan. A week later it introduced the 80386, its first 32-bit processor. Intel will concentrate on microprocessors; the chip industry is in its worst slump in years.
imageCaption: The Intel 386 microprocessor

headline: Reagan and Gorbachev meet in Geneva
text: US President Ronald Reagan and Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev met in Geneva from 19 to 21 November, the first US-Soviet summit since 1979. They agreed on no arms cuts, but their joint statement says a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought, and they agreed to meet again.
imageCaption: President Reagan and General Secretary Gorbachev at their first meeting, Geneva, 19 November 1985

headline: Philip Morris completes the 5.75 billion dollar purchase of General Foods
text: Philip Morris completed its takeover of General Foods, the maker of Maxwell House coffee, Jell-O and Kool-Aid, which it agreed in late September at 120 dollars a share, 5.75 billion dollars in all. It is the biggest takeover outside the oil industry so far and creates the largest consumer products company in the United States. This year Philip Morris is also passing Reynolds as the biggest US cigarette maker.
imageCaption: Maxwell House coffee plant, Jacksonville, Florida (a General Foods brand)

headline: Zurich ends a brilliant year with Nestlé at record highs
text: The Zurich stock exchange closed the year 'in brilliant form', the Neue Zürcher Zeitung wrote on 31 December: chemical shares were strong and Nestlé's shares again reached record prices. In September the five big industrial countries agreed at the Plaza Hotel in New York to push the dollar down, and a dollar now buys 2.06 francs, against 2.86 in February.
source: Neue Zürcher Zeitung, 31 December 1985, p. 17 ('Viel Glanz über dem Aktienmarkt'), scan data/manual/scans/nzz/NZZ_1985-12-31.pdf (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaza_Accord (read 2026-10-03); FRED DEXSZUS (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Traders at the ring of the Zurich stock exchange, 20 November 1985
imageCredit: Jules Vogt, Comet Photo AG (Zürich), ETH-Bibliothek Zürich, Bildarchiv

headline: 1985 in review: shares up 26 percent in a year of takeovers
text: The S&P 500 rose 26% in 1985 to 211.28 and first closed above 200 on 21 November. The Dow ended at 1,546.67, up 27.7%, after 36 record closes. Falling interest rates and the September agreement of the five big economies at the Plaza Hotel to push the dollar down helped shares, and takeover bids financed with borrowed money, often with high-yield 'junk' bonds sold by Drexel Burnham Lambert, have made many shareholders rich.
imageCaption: President Reagan addresses brokers and clerks at the New York Stock Exchange, 28 March 1985

headline: Disney picks France for Euro Disneyland
text: On 18 December Disney chose a site at Marne-la-Vallee, about 20 miles east of Paris, over Spain for a European Disneyland due to open in 1991. It could draw up to 10 million visitors a year and employ 10,000 people. French officials put the cost at 1.8 billion dollars, which Disney said 'sounds a little high'.
imageCaption: Disneyland Paris
